chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (the second Imam), peace be upon him: 'May I be your ransom, indeed a man from our companions threw the Jamarah on the Day of Nahr (sacrifice) and shaved [his head] before he slaughtered [his animal].'

He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was visited on the Day of Nahr by groups of Muslims who said: O Messenger of Allah, we slaughtered before we threw [the Jamarah] and we shaved before we slaughtered, so nothing remained of what ought to be advanced except that they delayed it, and nothing of what ought to be delayed except that they advanced it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: No harm, no harm.'

So there is in it nothing that contradicts what we mentioned, because in the apparent meaning of the report it is not indicated that they did that intentionally or forgetfully. So if that is not in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as being in the state of forgetfulness, and that which indicates that is what was narrated:

key_terms.لَا حَرَجَ: No harm / No blame (a legal declaration of permissibility despite irregularity)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Day of Nahr (the day of Eid al-Adha during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before slaughtering the sacrificial animal during Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi utilizes this narration to demonstrate the principle of *la haraj* (ease) in Hajj rituals, arguing that the Prophet’s declaration of 'no harm' applies even when the sequence of throwing Jamarat, slaughtering, and shaving is reversed. The scholar emphasizes that this ruling is derived from the apparent meaning of the text, which does not specify whether the companions acted intentionally or out of forgetfulness, thereby allowing for flexibility in the order of these essential acts (arkan) without invalidating the pilgrimage.
